entry_state: Inventory sales remove only the sold goods' allowance; recovery concerns goods still held. Net currency hedges retain gross sales, expenses and their recognition periods, with separate hedge presentation and reserve timing. The next section turns from hedging to employee award conditions, settlement rights and earnings participation.
exit_state: Award accounting distinguishes service and non-market conditions from market conditions, cash remeasurement from grant-date equity measurement, and the employee's settlement choice from the entity's. Beneficial amendments preserve original cost and add modification-date value over its own service period; cash-to-equity changes reconcile the existing liability rather than always adding a positive expense.
findings: The service-quantity example gives cumulative expenses 900,1600,2250 and annual charges 900,700,650; a failed market condition does not reverse the cost when other conditions are met.
Cash-settled remeasurement reaches 6750 at settlement; freezing the equity-award grant value would leave 4500 unrecorded.
Beneficial repricing uses same-date before/after values 2 and4, not grant-date3 versus current4. Additional instruments may have a different service period.
